_comment: Single source of truth for every upstream ref this repo indexes or mirrors.
FSM-App has THREE Frappe/ERPNext pins and they are not the same number - see the table in
FSM-App/CLAUDE.md § Version pins. `source` below is the PRODUCTION/CI pin, because that is
what shipped code runs against and therefore what a claim about 'the platform' must mean.
Do NOT point `source` at scripts/devcontainer-init.sh. That holds the devcontainer pin
(v16.20.0), which FSM-App's CLAUDE.md calls out as behind the other two - a known
divergence, not a target. Indexing it would make this repo answer confidently about a
platform production is not on, which is the exact failure it exists to prevent.
Note frappe/erpnext:vX.Y.Z is tagged with the ERPNext version, so the Frappe version inside
the production image differs from the image tag by design. These are per-repo tags, so the
pairing is explicit here and needs no inference.

source._comment: Production + CI. Enforced by ARG FRAPPE_VERSION in infrastructure/production/Dockerfile and FRAPPE_BRANCH/ERPNEXT_BRANCH in .github/workflows/ci.yml.

devcontainer._comment: What local dev runs, from FSM-App/scripts/devcontainer-init.sh. Behind production on purpose. index/drift.md reports what differs, so a 'works on my machine' gap is visible instead of surprising.

_comment: Frappe apps we do NOT install, indexed anyway and tagged installed:false.
Without these, `find_doctype` answers a bare 'not found' for anything they ship, which
reads as 'the platform cannot do this' - the exact wrong conclusion. It already cost us:
a mileage question was answered from recall about hrms because hrms was not indexed.
The useful answer is neither 'no' nor a false 'yes'. It is: not on your bench, but app X
ships it, here is its shape, so adopt-or-build becomes a real decision.
Only hrms publishes version-N branches; the rest release continuously against frappe
develop, so they are pinned by ref and the resolved SHA is recorded in the index.

hrms.why: Closest adjacent app: Employee, Timesheet, Leave, Attendance, Expense Claim, and the Vehicle Log / Vehicle Service pair ERPNext dropped when HR split out.

crm.why: Lead/Deal pipeline and communication logging, adjacent to Service Request intake.

helpdesk.why: Ticketing, SLA and agent assignment, adjacent to job dispatch and customer follow-up.

press.why: The app behind Frappe Cloud: Site, Bench, Server, Team, Subscription. It is the reference implementation of what orchestrator/ and provisioner/ do by hand, so it is the best available check against rebuilding tenant lifecycle from scratch.

vendor._comment: Doc sets that genuinely live in git, synced verbatim. Resolved SHAs land in vendor/_manifest.json.

_comment: docs.frappe.io is a Frappe Wiki site - the content is in that site's database, not a repo.
frappe/frappe_docs was archived in Dec 2021. So these subtrees are crawled, not cloned.
Note there is no v16 tree upstream: framework docs stop at v15, ERPNext has no versioned
current tree at all. For anything v16-specific the index/ layer is the only real answer.

excluded._comment: Recorded so nobody has to guess whether a gap is deliberate. Roughly 4,860 of the sitemap's 6,663 URLs are skipped.
excluded.superseded_versions: erpnext/v12, erpnext/v13, erpnext/v14, framework/v13, framework/v14 - about 4,600 pages. Stale text that would surface as confidently wrong search hits, which is the opposite of this repo's purpose. framework/v15 is kept because it is the last versioned framework tree and often carries detail the unversioned 'user' tree dropped.
excluded.other_verticals: lending, education, books, learning, school - about 191 pages. Separate Frappe products (loan management, school ERP, desktop accounting, LMS) with no bearing on field service.
excluded.non_technical: customer-guide, partner-guide, legal - about 68 pages. Frappe's own pricing, support and partner-programme material, not platform documentation.
excluded.wiki_v1: wiki/ - 11 pages, superseded by wiki-v2/, which carries the same routes. Every wiki/ URL renders without a #wiki-content body, so selecting them only produced permanent skips. Dropped after the 2026-08-18 crawl recorded all 11 failing.

known_upstream_gaps._comment: Sections where upstream itself is partly broken, so a smaller page count here is not a crawl defect. mirror/_manifest.json lists every skip with its reason.
known_upstream_gaps.cloud: 27 of 183 pages fail upstream, mostly HTTP 500 on /cloud/handbook/* and /cloud/faq/*.
